items.title: Audit current-behavior claims in root AGENTS.md against authoritative implementation and decision sources
items.context: Distinguish current normative instructions from explicitly labeled legacy background; record reproducible source and command evidence for consistency conclusions.

happy.desc: Build a claim-by-claim audit ledger for every root AGENTS.md statement that asserts current Proof-or-Stop behavior; each row names the exact AGENTS.md section, verdict, authoritative implementation, command registry, canonical role prompt or adopted decision source with a line reference, plus a reproducible repository-local CLI command and captured result wherever the claim is CLI-observable. The ledger contains no unsupported current-behavior conclusion. Persist the ledger and its evidence expectations in docs/audits/AGENTS-current-version-audit.md so a reviewer can inspect the RED and GREEN proof independently. WHY: consistency must be demonstrated from live authority rather than asserted from memory.

edge.desc: Classify every command, phase, role, artifact and example mentioned in AGENTS.md as current, compatibility-only or historical. Any command absent from `node bin/proof-or-stop.js help --full` is removed from active guidance or explicitly and locally labeled legacy or historical; no nonexistent command remains presented as an executable current instruction. WHY: retained background is acceptable only when a reader cannot mistake it for the current interface.

adversarial.desc: Mechanically enumerate every active `proof-or-stop` command example in AGENTS.md and verify it against the repository-local CLI version reported by `node bin/proof-or-stop.js --version`: every referenced command resolves and its `--help` succeeds, read-only examples execute with concrete repository-valid arguments, and mutating examples are exercised only in an isolated disposable repository or validated through the same registered command schema without changing this story. Include a deliberately malformed argument and prove that the checker rejects it. WHY: active examples must be operational and the audit must discriminate unsupported or malformed invocations instead of returning a false green.

items.userSees: The user sees "Audit evidence: PASS" with reproducible commands and source locations that distinguish current rules, compatibility background, and corrected inconsistencies.

verificationEvidence.note: The durable audit ledger maps all 26 baseline RED defects to exact current authorities, final English claims, GREEN receipts, and the 46197017 verifier commit.
Exact command-contract ledger reaches its final case, proving all 42 current CLI invocations were executed and accepted.

items.title: Translate the complete root AGENTS.md into English without semantic drift
items.context: Translate all Chinese prose, headings, table cells, comments, examples, and operator guidance while preserving code blocks, CLI commands, JSON keys, identifiers, paths, lifecycle semantics, and explicit legacy/current distinctions.

happy.desc: Translate every human-language surface in root AGENTS.md, including headings, prose, table cells, block quotes, HTML comments, code comments and example annotations, then scan the complete file and prove there are zero Unicode Han-script characters and zero U+FFFD replacement characters. Any remaining non-ASCII character must be an intentional language-neutral technical symbol rather than untranslated prose. WHY: a partial translation or corrupted replacement glyph does not satisfy the request for a fully English file.

edge.desc: Compare the translated file with the pre-change story baseline using a deterministic structural and token inventory: preserve Markdown hierarchy, list nesting, tables, block quotes, fenced-block boundaries and language tags, HTML-comment boundaries, links, paths, command and role identifiers, JSON keys, phase names, story IDs and other technical tokens, except where the consistency audit explicitly records removal or historical relabeling of an obsolete item. All intentional structural or token differences are listed and justified. WHY: English prose must not silently damage executable syntax or document structure.

adversarial.desc: Perform a focused semantic-drift review against the pre-translation text for every normative or lifecycle-sensitive sentence, especially MUST, MUST NOT, NEVER, only, current, legacy, advisory, blocking, phase transitions and actor authority. Prove the review detects representative mutations that invert a negation, change advisory to mandatory, or erase the current-versus-legacy qualifier; the final translation preserves polarity, modality, scope and exception boundaries. WHY: fluent English can still reverse a gate or workflow rule.

items.userSees: The user opens root AGENTS.md and sees a complete English document with no Chinese prose, replacement characters, or altered technical identifiers.

verificationEvidence.note: The final root AGENTS.md contains zero Han characters, replacement characters, and non-ASCII residues, proving complete English translation.

items.title: Verify translation completeness and current-version consistency with reproducible evidence
items.context: Use automated non-ASCII/CJK checks plus focused comparisons to current CLI help, registries, prompt assets, and authoritative decision documents; report any residual intentional non-English literals separately.

happy.desc: Produce reproducible final evidence that binds the audited AGENTS.md to the current repository state: record the CLI version and git HEAD, exact authoritative source references, exact commands, exit codes and salient outputs for the claim audit, translation-completeness scan, structural or technical-token comparison and command-example checks. A fresh reviewer can rerun the recorded commands from this worktree and reach the same pass or fail conclusions. Persist the evidence ledger and its rerun expectations in docs/audits/AGENTS-current-version-audit.md. WHY: the requested proof must be inspectable evidence, not a prose assurance.

edge.desc: Run whole-file Unicode checks rather than line samples: assert zero Han-script and U+FFFD characters, enumerate every remaining non-ASCII code point with line locations, and explicitly classify each residual as an intentional language-neutral technical symbol or fail the item. Also verify no mixed-language heading, table cell, comment or example was skipped. WHY: hidden residual text and replacement corruption commonly survive visual spot checks.

Record and separately report the repository-local worktree CLI and the globally resolved `proof-or-stop` runtime: capture each reported version plus the invoked path and canonical resolved realpath. Treat `node bin/proof-or-stop.js` from the B-d854 worktree as the authority for auditing current repository behavior and active examples; report any global version or path drift as a distinct environment finding without substituting the global runtime for local authority, concealing the drift, or treating unrelated global drift as proof that the worktree documentation is inconsistent. WHY: repository truth and host installation state are separate facts and the evidence must make that boundary reproducible.

adversarial.desc: Independently extract all active CLI examples from the final AGENTS.md and smoke them through `node bin/proof-or-stop.js`, using real read-only invocations and an isolated disposable repository or registered-schema validation for mutations. Cross-check command names against `help --full`, require explicit historical labeling for every unavailable command, and add a known-invalid or malformed argument that must fail the audit. The evidence must show all genuine active examples pass and the malformed invocation is rejected. WHY: a command checker that accepts both valid and invalid examples proves nothing.
